title: Rationalization of the specified completed-pullback unit
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Let $g:X'\to X$ be any morphism between schemes with the same scheme hypotheses. Define $B_{X'},E_{X'},\mathcal C_{X'},Q,J_{X'}$ in the same way. Let $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ be the coefficient map defined by its finite quotient projections, and put $P_gK=B_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}B_X}g^{-1}K$. Let $\widehat P_g$ and $\gamma_{g,K}:P_gK\to\widehat P_gK$ be exactly the completed pullback and quotient-tower completion unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Then $P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ for $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and $\gamma_{g,K}$ is an isomorphism. On pulled-back stratified perfect local models $B_S\otimes_A^LP$ the ordinary pullback has model $B_{S'}\otimes_A^LP$; completeness and the compatible etale witnesses are retained. These conclusions concern the specified unit, as in [lem-tw-ordinary-completed-integral-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. There is a natural comparison
$$\alpha_{g,QK}:J_{X'}(Q\widehat P_gK)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(J_XQK).$$
It is the composite of $J_{X'}(Q\gamma_{g,K}^{-1})$ with balanced tensor flattening; both ordinary sides identify with $E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}B_X}g^{-1}K$. The localization unit identification $g^{-1}E_X\cong(g^{-1}B_X)[1/\varpi]$ is the canonical one [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. The comparison descends to fraction morphisms and hence to a natural isomorphism on raw rationalizations. No isomorphism $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_{X'}$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, Lemma 6.5.9 and Remark 6.8.15, ordinary/completed module pullback and specified completion unit, pp. 50,54,62

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] to $K$: it has finite stratified perfect local $A$-models, and this characterization includes the compatible etale-origin witnesses. Apply [lem-tw-ordinary-pullback-stratified-models] to $g$ and those models. The inverse-image strata, omitting empty ones, form a finite constructible stratification of $X\prime$; the pulled covers are pro-etale covers, and the ordinary pullback of each model is $B_{S\prime}\otimes_A^L P$, computed termwise on its finite-projective representative. Apply the reverse characterization on $X\prime$. Thus $P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X\prime}$, including completeness, the uniform reduction bound and compatible etale witnesses. Both schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional and have $\ell$ invertible, as required by that characterization; no geometric assumption on $g$ beyond being a morphism is needed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11; ordinary pullback of stratified perfect models, Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: The rings $A/\varpi^n$ are finite [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], using the absolute value, discrete valuation ring and finite residue field of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to $g$ and the tower $(A/\varpi^n)_n$: its comparison is the unique map with the finite projection equations, hence equals $c_g$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and it is an isomorphism. This is proved there, not assumed; it also identifies the pulled finite coefficient sheaves and transitions with those of $X'$. So module pullback along $c_g$ is exact and $P_g$ is termwise pullback. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] to $g$ with $R_X=B_X$, $R_{X'}=B_{X'}$, this isomorphism and $Q_{X,\bullet}=((A/\varpi^n)_X)_n$. Its $B_X(K)$ is the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and its termwise pullback is $Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], which is levelwise module pullback on the same flat-term K-flat class. The natural isomorphism $\tau_K:Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet\to(P_gK)_\bullet$ satisfies $\tau_K\,Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(i_K)=i_{P_gK}$. By definition $\gamma_{g,K}$ is the constant-tower unit $P_gK\to R\lim\Delta P_gK$ followed by $R\lim Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}(i_K)$. Naturality of that unit and the augmentation equation give $R\lim(\tau_K)\circ\gamma_{g,K}=u_{P_gK}$, the constant-tower unit of $P_gK$ followed by $R\lim$ of its strict quotient augmentation. This is an equality of functorially induced maps, not an inference from projections. By Step 1, $P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ is intrinsically derived $\varpi$-complete [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], so [lem-weil-pbc-intrinsic-to-tower-complete] makes $u_{P_gK}$ invertible. Hence $\gamma_{g,K}$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K$ by naturality of $\tau$ and of the units, and $\widehat P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X'}$, which is closed under isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), Remark 6.8.15; completion unit of ordinary pullback of a complete constructible complex, via the strict reduction tower

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $T^\bullet\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Write $R=g^{-1}B_X$, $S=B_{X\prime}$, $U=E_{X\prime}$ and $N=g^{-1}T^\bullet$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence], $g^{-1}E_X=R[1/\varpi]$ canonically, preserving the unit, and inverse image and scalar localization are exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] successively to the inverse-image ringed topos with structural map $\mathrm{id}_R$, the coefficient change $R\to S$, and the localizations. Thus $N$, $S\otimes_R N$, $R[1/\varpi]\otimes_R N$, and their further scalar extensions are flat-term K-flat over their respective rings. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] computes the corresponding derived pullbacks by these complexes and makes their comparison maps independent of resolution. In particular both iterated derived tensors below can be computed by ordinary iterated tensors on these representatives.

By the object formula in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor], the ordinary integral side realizes to $J_{X\prime}(QP_gK)=U\otimes_S^L(S\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K)$. On the representatives of Step 3 its flattening to $U\otimes_R N$ sends $u\otimes(s\otimes n)$ to $us\otimes n$; its inverse sends $u\otimes n$ to $u\otimes(1\otimes n)$. These formulas respect both balancing relations, are mutually inverse and commute with differentials. They define a natural chain isomorphism and hence a natural derived isomorphism $a_K:J_{X\prime}(QP_gK)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; explicit balanced calculation on the K-flat representatives of Step 3

proof.text: Apply the localization comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] to $T^\bullet$. The other ordinary side is represented by $U\otimes_{R[1/\varpi]}(R[1/\varpi]\otimes_R N)$. The map to $U\otimes_R N$ sends $u\otimes(r/\varpi^m\otimes n)$ to $u\,c_g(r)\varpi^{-m}\otimes n$, and its inverse sends $u\otimes n$ to $u\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The extension of $c_g$ to $R[1/\varpi]\to U$ exists because $\varpi$ is invertible in $U$. The balancing and fraction relations show that these maps are well defined and inverse, and they commute with differentials and maps in $N$. Sheaf tensor is the sheafification of balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so the formulas give sheaf chain maps. Thus they give a natural derived isomorphism $b_K: E_{X\prime}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(J_XQK)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; the localization-unit-preserving identification and explicit balanced inverse

proof.text: Define $\alpha_{g,QK}=b_K^{-1}\circ a_K\circ J_{X\prime}(Q\gamma_{g,K}^{-1})$. Every factor is invertible by Steps 2, 4 and 5. Naturality of $\gamma$ and of the two chain comparisons gives, for every integral morphism $f:K\to L$, the equation $G(f)\alpha_{g,QK}=\alpha_{g,QL}H(f)$, where $H(K)=J_{X\prime}(Q\widehat P_gK)$ and $G(K)=E_{X\prime}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(J_XQK)$. This proves naturality on integral representatives and the asserted normalization through the inverse of the specified unit.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; elementary composition of the natural comparisons of Steps 2, 4 and 5

proof.text: The maps $c_g$ preserve constant $A$-scalars: their finite projections send each $a\in A$ to its constant residue. Thus [lem-pur-ringed-derived-pullback-linear] makes $P_g$ $A$-linear. Naturality of the invertible $B_{X\prime}$-linear maps $\gamma$ gives $\widehat P_g(f)=\gamma_{g,L}P_g(f)\gamma_{g,K}^{-1}$. Conjugating sums and scalar multiples by these maps proves that $\widehat P_g$ is $A$-linear as well. Extend it to [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] by $f/\varpi^n\mapsto\widehat P_g(f)/\varpi^n$. If $f/\varpi^n=h/\varpi^m$, some $r\geq0$ has $\varpi^r(\varpi^m f-\varpi^n h)=0$; applying this $A$-linear functor proves independence of representative, and the sum and composition formulas follow in the same way. By the fraction formula for $J$ in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor], both $H(f/\varpi^n)$ and $G(f/\varpi^n)$ are $\varpi^{-n}$ times the integral maps. Multiplying the naturality equation of Step 6 by $\varpi^{-n}$ proves it for every fraction. Hence $\alpha_g$ is the required natural isomorphism on raw rationalizations. All maps used $c_g$ and its localization; its invertibility is the proved statement cited in Step 2, never an assumption.
